cards.front: Strategy: work backwards
cards.back: Start from the end result and undo each step in reverse order. Example: I double a number and add 5 to get 17. Subtract 5 to get 12, then halve to get 6.
cards.say: Strategy: work backwards. Start from the end result and undo each step in reverse order. Example: I double a number and add five to get seventeen. Subtract five to get twelve, then halve to get six.

cards.front: Work backwards: I think of a number, multiply by 3, subtract 4 and get 20. Find it.
cards.back: 8. Undo the steps: 20 + 4 = 24, then 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
cards.say: Work backwards: I think of a number, multiply by three, subtract four and get twenty. Find it. Eight. Undo the steps: twenty plus four is twenty four, then twenty four divided by three is eight.

cards.front: Strategy: make a systematic list
cards.back: List every possibility in a fixed order so none is missed or repeated. Example: always start with the smallest first digit.
cards.say: Strategy: make a systematic list. List every possibility in a fixed order so none is missed or repeated. Example: always start with the smallest first digit.

cards.front: How many 2-digit numbers use the digits 1, 2 and 3 with no repeats?
cards.say: How many two digit numbers use the digits one, two and three with no repeats? Six. The numbers are twelve, thirteen, twenty one, twenty three, thirty one, thirty two.

cards.front: Strategy: use odd and even (parity)
cards.back: Odd + odd = even, even + even = even, odd + even = odd. This can show that something is impossible.
cards.say: Strategy: use odd and even, parity. Odd plus odd equals even, even plus even equals even, odd plus even equals odd. This can show that something is impossible.

cards.front: Can five odd numbers add up to 20?
cards.back: No. Odd + odd = even, so two odds make an even, four odds make an even, and the fifth odd makes the total odd. 20 is even.
cards.say: Can five odd numbers add up to twenty? No. Odd plus odd equals even, so two odds make an even, four odds make an even, and the fifth odd makes the total odd. Twenty is even.

cards.front: Strategy: use divisibility tricks
cards.back: Digit sum divisible by 3 means the number is divisible by 3. Digit sum divisible by 9 means divisible by 9. Even last digit means divisible by 2.
cards.say: Strategy: use divisibility tricks. Digit sum divisible by three means the number is divisible by three. Digit sum divisible by nine means divisible by nine. Even last digit means divisible by two.

cards.front: Is 4,725 divisible by 9?
cards.back: Yes. 4 + 7 + 2 + 5 = 18, and 18 is a multiple of 9.
cards.say: Is four thousand seven hundred and twenty five divisible by nine? Yes. Four plus seven plus two plus five equals eighteen, and eighteen is a multiple of nine.

cards.front: Strategy: the pigeonhole idea
cards.back: If there are more items than boxes, some box must hold at least two items.
cards.say: Strategy: the pigeonhole idea. If there are more items than boxes, some box must hold at least two items.

cards.front: 13 children. Must two of them have a birthday in the same month?
cards.back: Yes. There are only 12 months, so with 13 children at least two share a month.
cards.say: Thirteen children. Must two of them have a birthday in the same month? Yes. There are only twelve months, so with thirteen children at least two share a month.

cards.front: A drawer holds red, blue and green socks. How many must you take to be sure of a matching pair?
cards.back: 4. Three socks could be all different colours, but the 4th must match one of them.
cards.say: A drawer holds red, blue and green socks. How many must you take to be sure of a matching pair? Four. Three socks could be all different colours, but the fourth must match one of them.

cards.front: Strategy: think about the worst case
cards.back: Ask: what is the unluckiest thing that could happen? Then add one more.
cards.say: Strategy: think about the worst case. Ask: what is the unluckiest thing that could happen? Then add one more.

cards.front: A bag has 5 red and 5 blue marbles. How many must you take to be sure of 2 the same colour?
cards.back: 3. The first two might be different colours, but the third must match one of them.
cards.say: A bag has five red and five blue marbles. How many must you take to be sure of two the same colour? Three. The first two might be different colours, but the third must match one of them.

cards.front: Strategy: make it simpler
cards.back: Try a smaller version of the problem, find the pattern, then use it on the big version.
cards.say: Strategy: make it simpler. Try a smaller version of the problem, find the pattern, then use it on the big version.

cards.back: 55. Pair the ends: 1 + 10, 2 + 9, 3 + 8, 4 + 7, 5 + 6. Five pairs of 11 make 55.
cards.say: One plus two plus three plus four plus five plus six plus seven plus eight plus nine plus ten. Fifty five. Pair the ends: one and ten, two and nine, and so on. Five pairs of eleven make fifty five.

cards.front: A 10 m straight fence has a post every 2 m, with a post at each end. How many posts?
cards.back: 6 posts. Posts are at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 metres. There is always one more post than gaps.
cards.say: A ten metre straight fence has a post every two metres, with a post at each end. How many posts? Six. There is always one more post than gaps.

cards.front: Strategy: draw a diagram
cards.back: A quick picture or table can show relationships that are hard to hold in your head.
cards.say: Strategy: draw a diagram. A quick picture or table can show relationships that are hard to hold in your head.

cards.front: 20 children: 12 play football, 15 swim, and everyone does at least one. How many do both?
cards.back: 7. 12 + 15 = 27 counts the both-group twice, and 27 - 20 = 7.
cards.say: Twenty children: twelve play football, fifteen swim, and all do at least one. How many do both? Seven. Twelve plus fifteen is twenty seven, which counts the both group twice, so take away twenty.

cards.front: Strategy: guess, check and improve
cards.back: Make a sensible guess, test it, then adjust. Each try should get closer.
cards.say: Strategy: guess, check and improve. Make a sensible guess, test it, then adjust. Each try should get closer.

cards.front: Two numbers add to 20 and differ by 4. Find them.
cards.say: Two numbers add to twenty and differ by four. Find them. Twelve and eight. Try twelve plus eight equals twenty and twelve minus eight equals four.

cards.front: Strategy: look for a cycle in the last digit
cards.back: Powers and multiples often repeat their last digits in a cycle. Find the cycle, then jump ahead.
cards.say: Strategy: look for a cycle in the last digit. Powers and multiples often repeat their last digits in a cycle. Find the cycle, then jump ahead.

cards.front: Powers of 2 end in 2, 4, 8, 6, 2, 4, ... What is the last digit of 2 multiplied by itself 10 times?
cards.back: 4. The cycle 2, 4, 8, 6 has length 4. After 8 steps it restarts, and 10 is 2 steps further: 4. (2 to the power 10 is 1,024.)
cards.say: The last digits of powers of two go two, four, eight, six, and repeat. What is the last digit of two multiplied by itself ten times? Four. Two to the power of ten is one thousand and twenty four.

cards.front: 5 people each shake hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes?
cards.say: Five people each shake hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes? Ten. Four plus three plus two plus one equals ten.

cards.front: The mean of 4 numbers is 7. Three of them are 5, 6 and 8. Find the fourth.
cards.back: 9. The total must be 4 × 7 = 28, and 5 + 6 + 8 = 19, so the fourth is 28 - 19 = 9.
cards.say: The mean of four numbers is seven. Three of them are five, six and eight. Find the fourth. Nine. The total must be twenty eight and the three add to nineteen, so the fourth is nine.

cards.front: How many squares of any size are in a 2 by 2 grid of squares?
cards.back: 5. There are 4 small squares and 1 big square.
cards.say: How many squares of any size are in a two by two grid of squares? Five. There are four small squares and one big square.
